S. D. REGISTRY
S. B. D. 7423
24 7 36

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, FRIDAY, JULY 24, 1936

Breach Of Promise Action
Pends In British Court

Application By Counsel For Plaintiff Follows
Failure Of Mr. Sansom To File Defence; 10
Days' Extension Of Time Given

A breach of promise action in H.M. Supreme Court, the parties being Miss Nadia Vassievsky and Abraham Sansom, sub-inspector of the S.M.P., was the subject of an application before Judge Grant Jones yesterday when Mr. K. E. Newman, for the plaintiff, asked for judgment to be entered in favour of his client by default, the defendant having failed to file his statement of defence within the specified period.

It was later agreed that an extension of time for 10 days should be granted, Mr. H. A. Reeks, who is representing Mr. Sansom in the case, explaining that his client was in the Country Hospital, recovering from an operation for appendicitis.

Mr. Newman stated that his client was strictly entitled to enter judgment for the amount of the claim and costs, but he was content to ask for the delivery of the defence within seven days and for the costs of the present application, in any event.

Mr. Reeks said he was surprised by the application, as he was under the impression that Mr. Newman did not intend to press the motion. It was his submission that counsel could agree between themselves upon an extension of time, and he had received a letter from Mr. Newman, written on July 18, which asked for delivery of the defence within seven days, which gave him until July 25 to comply, that was to say, Saturday.

Visit To Hospital

He had been unable to take full instructions from Mr. Sansom, as he was in hospital. Counsel was not expected to visit a hospital to get instructions.

Judge Grant Jones: It is more your duty to visit a hospital than that a rule of court should be broken.

Mr. Newman said that his reply was received on July 20, and he had been under the impression that Mr. Reeks proposed to wait until his client came out of hospital before delivering the defence. He felt it was a hard case, stating that the application was decided upon.

pages.zh:
15496
上海公共租界工部局警务处
特别分部登记处
S. B. D. 7423
36年7月24日

《字林西报》，1936年7月24日，星期五

违婚约诉讼
待英国法院审理

原告律师在桑瑟姆先生未提交答辩状后提出申请；获准延期十天

昨日，格兰特·琼斯法官（Grant Jones）审理了一项申请，涉及纳迪亚·瓦西耶夫斯基小姐（Miss Nadia Vassievsky）与上海公共租界工部局副督察亚伯拉罕·桑瑟姆（Abraham Sansom）之间在英国最高法院提起的违婚约诉讼。原告代理律师K. E. 纽曼先生（Mr. K. E. Newman）请求因被告未在规定期限内提交答辩状而作出缺席判决，判其客户胜诉。

后经协商，同意给予十天延期。代表桑瑟姆先生出庭的H. A. 里克斯先生（Mr. H. A. Reeks）解释说，他的客户正在乡村医院（Country Hospital）接受阑尾炎手术后的康复治疗。

纽曼先生表示，他的客户完全有权就索赔金额及诉讼费用获得判决，但他满足于要求对方在七天内提交答辩状，并要求由对方承担本次申请的费用。

里克斯先生称对该申请感到惊讶，因为他原以为纽曼先生不打算坚持该动议。他陈述认为，双方律师可以自行商定延期事宜，且他收到过纽曼先生于7月18日写来的一封信，信中要求在七天内提交答辩状，这意味着截止日期为7月25日，即星期六。

探访医院

他未能从桑瑟姆先生处获得完整指示，因为后者正在住院。通常不期望律师前往医院获取指示。

格兰特·琼斯法官指出：比起违反法庭规则，前往医院才是你更应尽的职责。

纽曼先生说，他于7月20日收到了回复，且他原以为里克斯先生打算等到其客户出院后再提交答辩状。他觉得此案情形严苛，并表示该申请已获裁定。
